question: Which method was used for making bronze statues during Harrapan Civilisation ?
solution:
The correct answer is **'****__Lost Wax casting__'**. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **bronze statue** of a **dancing girl** from **Mohenjo-Daro** is a significant example of the prehistoric **Harappan Civilisation**.
 
• It was made using the technique known as** lost wax casting.**
 
• **Wax** is used to create a wax replica of the statue, which is then covered with a **cast** or mould.
 
• When the mould is **heated**, the wax drains out.
 
• The mould is then filled with **molten** **bronze**, which is then cooled.
 
• The metal statue is gradually revealed once the cast has been carefully broken.

Hence, the correct answer is **Lost Wax casting.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** Let's have a look at other options:

 
• **Stone carving**

 
 
• **​**Stone carving is an activity where pieces of rough **natural stone** are carefully removed and moulded.
 
• Stone carving is one of the processes which may be used by an artist when creating a sculpture.
 
 
 
• **Ivory carving**
 
 
• **​**Ivory carving is the process of carving ivory, which is an** animal tooth or tusk**, usually with the help of sharp cutting instruments that are operated manually or mechanically.
 
• Humans have ornamentally carved ivory since prehistoric times, it was usually a rare and expensive material used for luxury products.
 
 
 
• **Wood carving**
 
 
• ​Wood carving is a form of **woodworking** by means of a cutting tool (knife) in one hand or a chisel by two hands or with one hand on a chisel and one hand on a mallet, resulting in a wooden figure or image, or in the sculptural ornamentation of a wooden object.
 
• The making of sculpture in wood has been extremely widely practised,
